solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: The dead King lives, oddly

indicators.note: behaving oddly, the letters of the word lives are put into a strange new order

explanation.surface: A tabloid claim that the late rock-and-roll King is still alive, strangely enough.
explanation.walkthrough: 'oddly' looks as if it means alternate letters, but here it signals an anagram of LIVES.
explanation.definitionFit: Elvis Presley, nicknamed the King of Rock and Roll, died in 1977, hence the dead King.

clue.text: Love — nude and I get kinky in Worthing together

indicators.note: placed in the middle of the Worthing piece, which wraps around the rest

parts.note: Jack Worthing in Wilde's The Importance of Being Earnest is a Justice of the Peace, a JP
love is a zero score in tennis, a round letter O

indicators.note: letters that get kinky are twisted out of shape, so nude and I are rearranged

explanation.surface: A saucy scene: a lover and the speaker undressing and getting up to mischief in a seaside town together.
explanation.walkthrough: Worthing looks like the Sussex seaside town but is Jack Worthing of Wilde's play, a Justice of the Peace. 'get kinky' scrambles its fodder into INEDU, which follows the O.
explanation.definitionFit: Joined-up is an adjective meaning connected or co-ordinated, things acting together as one.

clue.text: Goes on stage

definitions.meaning: to get on a ship, train or bus is to board it
the theatre stage is known as the ..., as in treading the ...

explanation.surface: An actor makes an entrance onto the stage.
explanation.definitionFit: Boarding a train means going on it; actors on stage are said to tread the boards.

clue.text: Polish data is kept on it

definitions.meaning: to polish or smooth something with a rasp-like tool
a computer document or folder holding stored information

explanation.surface: A Polish computer record being described, as if data were stored on a nationality.
explanation.definitionFit: A file is both a smoothing tool's action on metal and a container for stored records.

clue.text: Married at the back of the boat, nameless commander

indicators.note: without a name, so the letter N standing for name is dropped

parts.words: at the back of the boat
parts.note: astern means at or towards the rear of a vessel

explanation.surface: A wedding held at the stern of a ship under an anonymous captain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'nameless' removes N (name) from ASTERN, leaving ASTER.
explanation.definitionFit: A ship's master is its captain, the one in command of the vessel.

clue.text: No more tigerish

parts.note: describes a creature so heavily marked with bands that nothing could be more like a tiger in its markings

explanation.surface: A comment that someone's tigerish days are over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'No more' looks like 'no longer', but read it as 'none more': the superlative of having bands, a tiger's trademark.
explanation.definitionFit: Tigers are famous for their bands, so the most tigerish creature is the one with the most bands.

clue.text: Lush chocolate bars Lawrence demolished, about fifty-one

indicators.note: the shuffled letters go round the Roman numerals
knocked down and rebuilt, so the remaining letters are shuffled
bars here means excludes, so those letters are kept out of the word chocolate

parts.note: T. E. Lawrence, Lawrence of Arabia, is known by his initials TE
L is fifty and I is one in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: Lawrence wolfs down rich chocolate bars, about fifty-one of them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lush' is a slang noun for a heavy drinker, not an adjective. The anagram of what is left after 'bars' gives ALCOHOC, which 'about' opens to take the Roman numerals.
explanation.definitionFit: A lush is slang for a habitual drunk, someone addicted to drink.

clue.text: Company knees-up

definitions.meaning: a group of people travelling or acting together
British slang for a lively celebration with dancing

explanation.surface: A firm's office celebration.
explanation.definitionFit: A party can be a group of people together, and also a celebration; a knees-up is British slang for a lively get-together.

clue.text: More like naturists, one's learnt

definitions.meaning: split as two words, naturists have less clothing on
something taught and learned, a unit of teaching

explanation.surface: A nudist realises they have learnt something about wearing fewer clothes.
explanation.walkthrough: Split the answer as LESS ON: naturists wear less.
explanation.definitionFit: A lesson is a thing a person learns, either a class or an experience that teaches.

clue.text: News one's passing on over evening meal?

indicators.note: the dier piece goes over and around the pair of letters

parts.note: someone who is dying, a dier
read as News, the plural of N for new: two Ns

explanation.surface: A broadcaster passing on the news over supper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'News' is not reporting but the plural of the abbreviation for new; 'one's passing on' is someone dying.
explanation.definitionFit: Dinner is the main meal, usually eaten in the evening; the question mark allows for lunchtime dinners.

clue.text: Potentially shocking vicious circle assimilating energy and time

indicators.note: a vicious circle here is a circle treated savagely, its letters mauled into a new order

parts.note: E is the physics symbol for energy
T is the physics symbol for time

explanation.surface: A dangerous spiral of events absorbing ever more energy and time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'vicious circle' reads as a phrase, but 'vicious' is the anagram signal, with 'assimilating' taking E and T into the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Something carrying a current is liable to give a shock, so electric fits potentially shocking.

clue.text: In circling, passed over European seaport

indicators.note: turning round, so the letters are read backwards
the answer is in the words, spanning passed and over

explanation.surface: A ship circles before sailing past a European port.
explanation.definitionFit: Odessa is a major Black Sea port city in Ukraine.

clue.text: Engagement ring presented by unsupported Frenchman in Carmen

indicators.note: the shortened name sits inside the AA

parts.note: read as car men, the AA, Britain's Automobile Association

indicators.note: in a down clue the bottom letter holds the word up, so it is removed

parts.note: René is a typical French man's name

explanation.surface: An engagement ring given by a Frenchman in the opera Carmen.
explanation.walkthrough: Carmen looks like Bizet's opera but is car men, the AA (Automobile Association, a British breakdown service). 'unsupported' drops the last E of RENE.
explanation.definitionFit: An arena is a ring where combatants engage, such as gladiators fighting.

clue.text: Strictly speaking as the crow flies

indicators.note: spoken, so the word is matched with another that is pronounced identically

parts.note: the crow's flight path is a direct line

explanation.surface: A pedant insisting that, strictly speaking, distance should be measured as the crow flies.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Strictly speaking' reads as a phrase, but 'Strictly' is the definition and 'speaking' the sound signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Strait is an old adverb meaning strictly or tightly, as in strait-laced.

clue.text: All is ok (as suffering blood condition)

indicators.note: suffering letters are in a bad way, thrown into disorder

explanation.surface: A patient reassured that all is fine, despite having a blood disorder.
explanation.walkthrough: The bracket hides that 'suffering' scrambles ALL IS OK AS.
explanation.definitionFit: Alkalosis is a medical state in which the blood and body fluids become too alkaline.

clue.text: Cut off high speed punch

definitions.meaning: a fast pace, as in going at a fair lick
a sharp blow, as in a clout round the ear

explanation.surface: A boxer's quick blow severs something.
explanation.definitionFit: Clip means to trim, a rapid pace, and a smack, three separate senses of one word.

clue.text: Fashion designer sustaining ankle injury

indicators.note: the words ankle injury hold up and contain the name within them

explanation.surface: A couturier hurts their foot on the catwalk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sustaining' reads as suffering an injury but means holding inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Calvin Klein is an American fashion designer and brand.

clue.text: Having no alcohol in leek-stewing vessel

indicators.note: the teetotal letters sit inside the shuffled leek
stewed, the vegetable's letters are cooked into a new arrangement

parts.note: TT stands for teetotal

explanation.surface: A teetotal cook stewing leeks in a pot without wine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stewing' rearranges the vegetable into KELE, which is split to hold the teetotal abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: A kettle is a container for boiling water, a kind of vessel.

clue.text: Ultimately forget to request piece of work

indicators.note: at the very end, so only the final letter of forget is used

parts.note: to request is to ask

explanation.surface: Someone told to forget about asking for a job.
explanation.definitionFit: A task is a job or assignment to be done.

clue.text: Not, presumably, Henry VIII's judgment!

definitions.meaning: Henry VIII, famously stout, was presumably not a slim monarch
an opinion or view, as in to my mind

explanation.surface: A historian's verdict on Henry VIII.
explanation.walkthrough: Split the answer as THIN KING; the portly Tudor was presumably no such thing.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone's thinking is their opinion or reasoning on a matter, their view.

clue.text: East London journo wearing black coat

indicators.note: the black piece is worn around the journalist

parts.note: jet is a deep glossy black

indicators.note: in the Cockney speech of East London the H is dropped

parts.note: a hack is a journalist

explanation.surface: A Cockney reporter dressed in a black coat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'East London' drops the initial H, as Cockney speech does, leaving ACK.
explanation.definitionFit: A jacket is a short coat.

clue.text: Youngster gets Christopher dinner

parts.note: Kit is a familiar short form of the name Christopher
the clue as set read 10 here, a cross-reference to the light whose answer is dinner; the number ten is used

explanation.surface: A child being given a meal by Christopher.
explanation.walkthrough: As set the clue said 'Christopher 10'; the reference was printed as the answer to 10-across, but the wordplay wants the number itself.
explanation.definitionFit: A kitten is a young cat, so it is a youngster in the animal world.

clue.text: Particular hate — some rich interiors

indicators.note: the insides of each word, without its outer letters

explanation.surface: A fussy person despising some lavish home decor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Particular' means fussy in the surface but 'of particles' in the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Atomic relates to particles of matter, a whimsical reading of particular as of particles.

clue.text: Express disapproval of aim

explanation.surface: Protesting at someone's goal.
explanation.definitionFit: To object is to protest; an object is a purpose, as in the object of the exercise.

clue.text: The other side broadcasting music issue

indicators.note: broadcast over the air, so it is the spoken letters that count

parts.note: an issue of NME, the New Musical Express, a British music weekly

explanation.surface: Opponents airing a music controversy.
explanation.walkthrough: NME (New Musical Express, a British music paper) said as letters gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: The enemy is the opposing force in a war, those on the opposite team.

clue.text: Comic sot tripping over one of strings

indicators.note: the instrument is laid over and around the scrambled letters

parts.note: the cello is one of the string section

indicators.note: stumbling, so the drunk's letters fall into disorder

explanation.surface: A drunk stumbles over a cellist in the orchestra.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tripping' rearranges the drunk's letters into OST; 'Comic' is a noun, a comedian.
explanation.definitionFit: Lou Costello was the American comedian of the double act Abbott and Costello.

clue.text: Just missing company, with regular exceptions

indicators.note: letters are excepted at a regular interval, every third one starting from the first

parts.note: lacking companions, so lonely

explanation.surface: Simply lacking company, apart from occasional visits.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with regular exceptions' removes the first and fourth letters, L and E, three apart.
explanation.definitionFit: Only means merely, as in just a little or only a little.

clue.text: Not serious exercise in which family indulges

indicators.note: the family is held within the exercise, as one indulges or takes it in

parts.note: to jog is to run for exercise
kin are relatives

explanation.surface: A family casually going for a run, not taking it seriously.
explanation.definitionFit: Joking means jesting, the opposite of earnest.

clue.text: The punishment of young age or of old age after nearly full retirement

indicators.note: retiring is drawing back, so the letters are read in reverse
nearly all of the word, so its last letter goes

parts.note: senile describes the infirmity of the old

explanation.surface: Musing on punishments suffered in youth or in old age.
explanation.walkthrough: 'nearly full' shortens SENILE to SENIL; 'retirement' turns it round.
explanation.definitionFit: Lines are a schoolroom punishment, copying a sentence out many times, given to the young.

clue.text: Ample boobs cradling top novelist's head? That might be Alice or Virginia!

definitions.text: That might be Alice or Virginia!

indicators.note: the scrambled letters hold the rest in their arms
boobs means blunders, so the letters of ample are messed up

parts.note: ace means first-rate, top

indicators.note: the leading letter of novelist's

explanation.surface: A cheeky description of a buxom heroine embracing a famous author.
explanation.walkthrough: 'boobs' is a verb, blunders, giving PLAME around the rest. Alice Springs is an Australian town and Virginia a US state named after the Virgin Queen.
explanation.definitionFit: Alice (Springs) and Virginia are names of places, so each might be a geographical name.
